_readme_jobs: A-29: a line's "trade" can name a job (FolkJob: Smith, Baker, Healer, Herder, Farmer, Trader, Guard, Fisher, RoostKeeper, Tanner, Forager, PoolFisher...) as well as a task; folk with a job say a line from its pool most of the time, in talk and to the player. "mood": Cheerful, Plain or Grumpy (from the folk, or Grumpy/Cheerful when wary/warm of the player).
_readme: What folk say as you walk by. Edit freely while the game runs: it is read again a second after you save.
cultures: one entry per species name (Human, HumanChild, Dwarf, Elf, Goblin, Ogre, Hermit), then the species it is based on, then Any.
words: lists the {slots} pick from. A culture's own list wins over Any's. Words may hold slots of their own.

lines: a plain string, or an object: text, and optionally when (day, night, dawn, morning, afternoon, evening), trade (one or a list), weight (default 1), emote (Wave, Bow, Cheer, Dance: an answer to it, never said walking by).
Built-in slots: {trade} (from the words trade.Hammer, trade.Fish...), {home_town}, {species}, {player} (your body), {time_of_day} (or the words time.morning...).
A line whose slot can't be filled (no home town, out on the road) is skipped. town_start + town_end name each town.
Unknown keys are kept for later (dialogue options), so adding them does no harm.

lines.text: Back to the forge with me.
The road's long but it's good.
No need to bow to me.
Good to see one of our own.
Bread's in the oven, mind the heat.
First loaves were out before dawn.
Everyone wants bread, nobody wants to knead.
The hearth's hot enough for another batch.
Honey cakes later, if the bees allow.
Sit a while, you look worn through.
Willow bark for the ache, nettle for the rest.
Another scraped knee from the woodpile.
If one more fool walks into a beehive...
Herbs dry best in a {weather_word} wind.
That one always strays to the hedge.
Easy now, they spook at strangers.
Muddy pen, muddy boots, muddy everything.
Fences hold the beasts, not the foxes.
Plant in spring, ache all summer.
Look, don't touch. Unless you're buying.
Got this from a traveller up the road.
Keep to the paths after dark.
Wolves were seen past the ridge.
Quiet watch is a good watch.
I walk this round a hundred times a day.
Fish are deep when the sun's high.
Caught one this long! Well, nearly.
Lost another hook to that log.
Quiet now, you'll scare them off.
Eel for supper, if I'm lucky.
Bring me iron and I'll make it useful.
Strike while it glows, that's the trick.
Lovely ring to the anvil today.
Bent nails, bent tools, bent patience.
My back's not what it was.
Stack it bark up, or it rots.
Everyone comes by the well sooner or later.
Someone dropped a bucket in. Again.
Deep and cold, the way a well should be.
Who goes there? Oh, just you.
I see everyone who comes into {home_town}.
Nobody's come up the road all {time_of_day}.
A {player}! What can I sell you?
Lost a whole day to one hare.
The deer know my step by now.
There's a seam down there, I can feel it.
Mind your head in the low bits.
The pods sway when the colony dreams.
Silk stalks need checking every dusk.
All roosts full, all sleepers safe.
Scrape, stretch, hang. Scrape, stretch, hang.
This one will make a fine wrap.
The smell? You stop noticing. Mostly.
The rack holds three if you're careful.
Cave damp is the enemy of leather.
Moths by the glow, beetles by the walls.
Basket's half full. Out again soon.
Nothing out there but cold stone.
Never forage near the mouth by day.
Pale fish in the white pool, blind as stones.
Feel the ripples, not the light.
The pool gives what it gives.

lines: Not many come through {home_town} these days.

lines.text: Keep your hands where I can see them.
Quiet night. Let's keep it that way.
A {player}. Keep your hands where I can see them.
Hm. {player}s don't usually come this way.
Proper dwarf steel, this. None of that soft stuff.
A dwarf's bread could stop an arrow.
Tunnel rats in the grain stores. Again.
Gold's heavy, but it sells light.

lines: You stand in {home_town}. Wipe your feet.

lines.text: A proper bow. Your beard does you credit.
To the forge and the stone!
An elf! Mind the low ceilings, beanpole.
Pointy ears, soft hands. Ever lifted a hammer, {player}?
A bow from an elf? Call it even.
Wave all you like, it won't make you taller.
A human. Count your fingers after, {player}.
Tall folk. Always in a hurry.
Off with you, {player}. I've work to do.
The trees lend us their fallen wood. We only take that.
Moonflower and dew, the old cure.
Even the fish sing, if you listen.
Our herds wander where they please.
Elven bread keeps for a season.
Crude coin. We trade in favours here.

lines: The trees of {home_town} are old. Older than you.

lines.text: My arrows fly true. Keep that in mind.
You dance like a sapling in a gale.
A dwarf, above ground? Did the tunnels run out?
Careful, {player}. The trees here are older than your beard.
Stout as ever. Do try not to trample the moss.
Oh, a bow. How very... sturdy of you.
Yes, yes, we see you down there.
A {player}. You are far from your fields.
Stay back or I'll bonk you.
Big one. Ogre-thing. Not too close.

lines: Too small to eat. Go away.

lines.text: Little sneaky {player}. Hands off ogre stuff.

lines: Nobody comes out here. Why are you here?

lines.text: Quiet out here. I like it quiet.

lines: Mmm. Do not hurry. The mountain does not.
I have seen this snow fall many times. It is always new.
You walk so fast. Where is it all going?
The old songs keep the igloos warm.

lines.text: Three hundred winters on this shell, and still it itches.
The runes glow brighter when the cold comes. They remember.
Sit a while. There is no shame in sitting.
Mm? I was not asleep. I was listening to the ice.
In my day the drifts came up to the dome tops. Twice.
The fish below are patient. So am I.
Cold hands, cold line, cold fish. As it should be.
Each block is cut slow. A slow wall stands long.
Clear ice, this. You can see the old snow inside it.
Another crack in the north wall. Always the north wall.
The pale fire burns no wood. Only a little of me.
Warm your hands, quick one. It does not bite.
Do not breathe on it. It sulks.
The stars are out. Time to go in, slowly.
Late, late. Even the old ones sleep.
Morning light on the snow. Mmm.
Mmm. A wave. I will wave back, in a moment.
A bow! Few remember the old courtesies.
Such energy. I remember having that.
Mm. You have the look of someone who breaks things, {player}.
I have outlived many rude ones. I will outlive you.

lines: You're new. I can tell. You still flicker.
Do you remember your name? I've lost mine.
They walk right through us, you know.
Cold tonight. Or is it always?

lines.text: The living are asleep. The night is ours.
Have you found your way back yet? Nor have I.

_readme: What folk say when the player talks to them (A-93): the talk window lists the topics and a folk answers each from these lines. Read again a second after you save, like the rest of this file.

topics: each topic's id and the words the player picks. Relabel any of them here. To add a topic, give it an id and a label here and lines under it below; it shows before goodbye with no code change. The built-in ids are who, how, work, town, news, favour, help and bye; meet is an animal player's (beastTalk).

Then one entry per culture (Any, or a species name as in cultures), each topic a list of lines. A folk picks from its species' lines, its body's, then Any's (Any's count for less when its own culture has a fitting line). Words and built-in slots come from cultures above: {trade}, {home_town}, {player}, {time_of_day}, a culture's {culture_greeting}. {quest} is the quest the folk wants done, in a few words.

To add a line: append a string, or an object with text and any of the keys below. A line fits only when every key it has matches; a line with more keys is likelier, and a line that names the folk's state (tired, hungry, the weather) wins over one that doesn't, so how-are-you is honest.
Traits (each low, mid or high, or a list): warmth (cold to kind), trust, curiosity, courage, pride, beasts (fears animals to loves them).

state: tired, busy, hungry, thirsty, lonely, scared, hurt, weather (a list; !busy for not). weather: Hot, Dry, Cold, Rain, Snow, Storm, Bright, Wind. mood: Cheerful, Plain, Grumpy (its temper today). stance: Kin, Warm, Rival, Wary, Annoyed. trade: a job (Smith, Baker, Farmer...) or task. when: day, night, dawn, morning, afternoon, evening.

true or false: home (lives in a town), job (has one), need (wants a quest done), willing (will do a favour: trust and warmth against stance and how often it was asked lately), pestered (asked twice in the last few minutes: never willing then).

gesture: an emote it makes (Wave, Bow, Cheer, Dance, Pet, LookAround...) or a word the talk window shows. offer: quest, item:<item name>, directions, rumour:<what about>, discount:<percent>, refuses. ends: true closes the talk. weight: default 1.

who.text: A {trade}, from {home_town}.
Who's asking?
None of your business.
I'm the best {trade} you'll meet, that's who.
Oh, nobody you'd have heard of.
Born in {home_town}, never left. Never wanted to.
Someone who'd rather ask the questions. Where are you from?
A friend, if you'll have one.
Me? I keep {home_town} running, near enough.
Just someone on the road.
I, er... I'd rather not say.
A {trade}. Proud of it, too.
Glad you asked! I'm a {trade}, here in {home_town}.
Someone with work to do. Make it quick.
What, you don't know? Everyone knows me.

how.text: Never better. Lovely day for it.
Why do you want to know?
Better for the company. Nobody stops to talk any more.
Worn out. I could sleep standing up.
Starving. I haven't eaten since dawn.
Parched. Is there a well near?
Busy, but I've a moment for you.
Up to my ears in work, thanks for asking.
Something spooked the others. I'm keeping watch.
Lonely, truth be told. Thank you for stopping.
On my own too much. Not that I mind. Much.
Freezing. I can't feel my fingers.
Not in this storm! Get under a roof!
The glare's giving me a headache.

work: Bit of this, bit of that.

work.text: I'm a {trade}.
I'm a {trade}, and I love it.
Same work as yesterday. I'm a {trade}.
Nobody in {home_town} does it better. I'm the {trade}.
Looking for work, if you hear of any.
This and that. Mostly I watch people. Like you.
Hammer and tongs, all day long.
Bread before dawn, every day.
The fields don't plough themselves.
Fish. Mostly waiting for fish.
Keeping the peace. Mostly from goats.
Mending cuts and bad tempers.
Counting sheep. Wide awake.
Buying low, selling... well, selling.
Trees. Chop. Repeat.
Down in the dark, digging.
Tracking. Quietly. You're not helping.
Walking, mostly. The road's my work.

town.text: {home_town}'s the best town on the island. Ask anyone.
Everyone in {home_town} knows everyone's business. Mine's knowing it first.
Quiet place, {home_town}. I like it quiet.
No town for me. The road's my home.

news.text: Wouldn't tell you if there was.
They say there's a cave in the hills nobody comes back from the same.
One of the stone giants moved, out past the hills. Only a little. I swear it.
A traveller came through with tales of a ruin in the woods. Treasure, he said.
Wolves have been seen near the road. Keep to the light.
Prices are up. That's the news.
The fish moved upriver. Nobody knows why.
Somebody's been taking more than their share of firewood. I have my suspicions.

favour.text: Sorry, I can't help you.
Help yourself. Somewhere else.
I don't do favours for strangers.
I... no, I'd better not.
You again? No.
I've given you all I can spare, friend. Come back another day.
Ask someone else for a while.
Here, take a few berries for the road.
The town's that way. Follow the road.
Take a coin. Don't spend it all at once.
I suppose I can spare something. Here.
Tell you what: there's a cave up in the hills worth a look. Don't say I told you.
For you? A tenth off, if you buy today.
Call it a friend's price.
Have a fish. Caught this morning.
Mushrooms. The good kind, I promise.

help.text: Kind of you to ask, but no.
I can manage myself, thank you.
Well, if you're offering, you could {quest}.
Hmm. Can I trust you? Fine: you could {quest}.
I'd do it myself, but you could {quest}.
I daren't go myself. Could you {quest}?

bye.text: Do come back and tell me what you find.

who.text: {culture_greeting}. A {trade} of {home_town}, at your service.

town.text: {home_town} has stood since my grandmother's grandmother. Mind the mud.

who.text: I'm not supposed to talk to strangers!
I live in {home_town}! Do you want to see a frog?

how.text: Not sleepy. Not even a little.

town.text: {home_town} has a big dog. He's my friend.

news: There's a monster in the well. Probably.

news.text: I saw a stone giant once. It winked.

favour.text: You can have my best stick.
No! Mine!

who.text: {culture_greeting}. A {trade} of {home_town}, and that's enough.
A dwarf. What more is there to know?

how.text: My beard's damp and my ale's warm. How d'you think?

work.text: Stone and steel. What else is there?

town.text: {home_town} was dug by my grandsire's grandsire. Every stone by hand.

news.text: The deep veins are singing. Means there's silver down there.

favour.text: Dwarf steel at a fair price. Fair for a dwarf, mind.

who.text: {culture_greeting}. I tend the trees of {home_town}.
Older than I look. Younger than the oaks.

how.text: The leaves are glad today, so I am too.
The wind brings bad news from the east.

town.text: {home_town} grows where the trees allow. We ask before we build.

news.text: The old shrine in the wood has woken. The birds have gone quiet near it.

favour.text: Follow the stream and keep the moss on your left.

who.text: Who wants to know? You got shinies?

how: Sneaky. Very sneaky. You didn't see me.

news.text: Big folk got cheese in the cellar. Lots. Not that I looked.

favour.text: Shiny? No. Mine. ...fine, have a berry.

who.text: Me {trade}. Good {trade}.

who: Old. Older than the igloos. Not so old as the mountain.

who.text: A {trade}, these last two hundred winters.

how.text: Slow and warm. That is all one needs.

work.text: Fish below, ice above, fire between. That is the work.

town: We built the domes when the glacier was young. One block a day.

news.text: The runes on the old stones flicker at night. Something stirs under the ice.
The water's tasted strange since the last storm. Something upstream.

_readme: What folk say and do when the player comes up to them in an animal's body (A-93 row 3). Read like conversation above: one entry per culture (Any, or a species name), each topic a list of lines, the same keys (traits, state, stance, mood, when, gesture, offer, weight...).

The topics are how the folk takes the animal: pet (fond of it), puzzled (a tame beast that seems to want something), wary, scared, repelled (rats, spiders, slimes), awed (big or rare creatures); and bye. The code picks the reaction from the animal's group, then the folk's persona (beasts, courage, curiosity) and stance; the lines say it.

groups: which group each species is in, by its asset name, for species the code would place wrongly. The code's own groups: pet (Friendly), vermin (spins webs), predator (driven off, or a hunter of 20 kg or more), big (600 kg or more), livestock (hooves), small (under 15 kg), beast (the rest). A new group name here is taken as puzzling, except awe, which awes.

Two more keys for a line: group (the animal's groups it fits: "group": "livestock" or ["small", "pet"]) and response, what the folk then does with what the brain already does: approach, feed (comes closer with the line's offer, which must be an item), backoff, flee or none. Without one: pet approaches, wary and repelled back off, scared flees, puzzled and awed stay.
{player} is the animal, in lower case: "a {player}" reads "a wolf".

pet.text: Aww, look at you! Who's a good {player}?
Hello, little one. Lost, are you?
Here, have a berry. Don't tell anyone.
You're a fine one. Whose are you?
Ha! You want a scratch? Come here.
Oh, you're soft. Off you go now.
Shh, you'll wake the whole street. Come on.
You've come to the right one. I've a soft spot for strays.

puzzled.text: Hm? What do you want, little one?
Hm? What is it? What do you want?
A {player}, right up to me? Are you tame?
You're staring. I haven't got anything. Look, empty hands.
Odd. Animals don't usually come this close.
Well, don't just stand there. Go on, shoo.
Are you hungry? Is that it?
Not now, I'm working. Go find your herd.
Strange beast. You look at me like you know something.

wary.text: Easy now. Stay where you are.
I don't trust that look in your eye, {player}.
Slowly... nobody needs to get bitten.
Hah! I've seen off bigger than you.
Mind your teeth and I'll mind mine.

scared.text: Get away! Get away from me!
Wolves in the streets now? I'm off!
Don't eat me, I'm all bones!

repelled.text: Don't you dare crawl on me.
Where's a broom when you need one?
Horrible thing. Go back under your rock.
I'm not scared of you. I just don't like you.
Off the path, you. Go on.

awed.text: By the stars... look at the size of you.
I've heard of your kind. Never thought I'd see one.
Wait till I tell them at home. Nobody will believe me.
Bless you, great one. Pass in peace.

pet.text: A {player}! Can I keep it? Can I? Please?
It likes me! Look, it likes me!

puzzled: Are you lost? Where's your mum?
repelled: Ewww! It's so gross! ...can I poke it?

awed.text: Woooah. You're the biggest thing I ever saw.

pet.text: Hah, a stout little beast. You'd do well in the mines.

wary.text: Keep your distance, beast. My axe is never far.

scared: Under the mountain we'd have walls for this!

repelled.text: Cave vermin. Out of my way before I stamp on you.

awed.text: The old songs speak of beasts like you. Stone keep you.

pet.text: Peace, little sister of the woods. Rest a while.

puzzled: You've wandered far from the green. What troubles you?
wary: I see you, hunter. Let us both pass in peace.
repelled: Even you have a place in the world. Just not here.

awed.text: An elder of the wild. We are honoured.

pet: Food? You food? ...no. You friend. Maybe.
puzzled: What you want? You got shinies? No? Go.
wary: Mine! All mine! You no take!

scared.text: Aaah! Not eat goblin! Goblin stringy!

scared: Ogre not scared! ...ogre little bit scared.

pet.text: Mmm. A small warm thing. Rest by the fire, little one.

puzzled: You look at me as if I know something. I usually do.
awed: Ah. An old one, like me.

pet: Only the animals come by. Suits me. Sit, if you like.
puzzled: You too, eh? Come to stare at the old fool?
bye: Go on. The woods are yours more than mine.
